title: The Rooms We Learn to Want
sentences: Every flat I have lived in has taught me something about space.
The first was small enough that I could reach the kitchen from bed.
I assumed at the time that I simply needed somewhere larger.
The larger place, when I got it, was strangely uncomfortable.
Rooms that nobody used made the whole flat feel unfinished.
What I had actually wanted was a door I could close, not more area.
Estate agents describe property almost entirely in numbers.
Those numbers say nothing about where light falls in the afternoon.
They cannot express how a corridor makes a household behave.
We buy square metres and then spend years learning what we needed instead.
